transcript.text: To help me narrow this down, I need to know exactly what 'not working properly' means. Is one specific zone not heating up, or are none of them working? Also, many hobs have a child safety lock (often shown as a key or padlock symbol) that disables the controls. Was there a lock icon lit up on your display? If so, did you try holding that button for a few seconds to unlock it?
just the rear right ring isn't heating, the other three are fine. no lock symbol that I noticed, the display shows a number for it as normal

Thanks for clarifying. We need to determine if this is an induction hob or a standard ceramic/halogen one, as the cause differs. If it is induction: many zones will not heat at all if the pan isn't magnetic (like some aluminium or copper pans). The hob detects the wrong pan and stays off. If you put a steel pan that works on the other zones onto this rear right ring and it still doesn't heat, then there may be a fault with that zone's internal power module or coil. If it is ceramic/halogen: a single dead zone usually points to a failed heating element under the glass for that specific ring, or potentially a control switch issue. Please try the pan test I mentioned above and let me know if it heats up. Also, please confirm whether your hob is induction or ceramic.

It's a ceramic one, the flat glass type with touch controls, not induction. It's a Zanussi. It doesn't glow red at all on that ring, and it was slow to heat for a while before it stopped. I also noticed a slight burnt smell from that ring once a couple of weeks ago, but not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. On ceramic hobs, the element sits under the glass; when it burns out, that specific ring stops working while the others remain fine. For your safety, please do not use this hob again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Internal repairs on hobs involve mains voltage and high-temperature components that are not safe for DIY repair. You will need to contact an appliance engineer to check the faulty element (and check any associated wiring) for the rear right zone.
